note: Round-2 retest card, frozen before any model forward pass of the round-2 graph. Authority: owner ruling 2026-11-08 option 2 (revise the control statistic under a new pre-registration, then run W1 round 2). Round 1's layered attribution (rank/value fixed; pairwise blocked by content-feature discriminability; alignment blocked by the untied read query) directly motivates the two design changes below; both failure layers are fixed in ONE round per the cap-higher mainline policy.

design.inherits_round1: the round-1 content pathway is retained verbatim: k = unit_ball(unit_ball(raw_key) + gain * unit_ball(P c)), P = shared 32x128 projection (seed 20261031), gain = 1.0
design.change_1_centered_content_feature: the content feature becomes c = normalize(bc(q) - centroid), where bc(q) is the 128-dim byte-count vector of the step's goal text and centroid = the mean of bc over the 22 probe-face query texts (INPUT-SIDE statistics only; no gold, no answers, no scoring data are touched). Rationale: round 1 measured that template sharing across the 22 questions drowns the slot-value discrimination of the raw byte-count feature (pairwise separable fraction 0.1039). Centering removes the common mode so the feature carries each question's DISTINCT bytes. Fallback: if the centered vector has zero norm for some input (a query identical to the centroid), the plain normalized byte-count is used for that input. Deployment note, pinned honestly: the centroid is a fixture-level input-side statistic for this zero-training function-class test; a running-input centroid estimator is a deployment concern outside this window.
design.change_2_tied_read_query: the read query gets the SAME content boost with the SAME projection and gain: q = unit_ball(unit_ball(raw_query) + gain * unit_ball(P c)). Rationale: round 1 measured query_alignment -0.139 (write and read subspaces near-orthogonal); the shared content component ties the two pathways, which is exactly the 'smallest sufficient fix' the manifest names for query_key_misaligned. The trace's fast_queries become post-injection; the query_alignment statistic therefore measures the tied pathways as deployed.
design.projection: the SAME P instance serves write keys and read queries (weight tying at the content pathway); P remains trainable for any subsequent bounded training window

graph.base_builder: probe_taiji_package20_4c_r2_formal_comparison.build_graph(candidate, gate, arm) (sha 112c76ae...), NO checkpoint load - round 2, like round 1, evaluates the modified graph at initialization (the parent attribution showed collapse already at init, so init is the correct function-class state)
graph.enable: taiji.rule_learning_20_1_net.enable_content_keys(graph, seed=20261031, centroid=<mean byte-count of the 22 probe-face queries>): registers P, swaps the frozen config via dataclasses.replace(content_keys_enabled=True, content_centered=True, content_gain=1.0), registers the centroid as a non-trainable buffer
